questions.block: This lane cannot open its declared era 1 because two live rulings assign feature 078 to two different lanes.
background: Q-GLPNETA16-12 (ariellas-glpnet, 2026-09-01) made 078 verification-receipts this lane's era 1 and described it as 'ship + close only'.
Q-GLPNETS15-02 (gavriella-glpnet, 2026-09-02T14:20Z) assigns 078 to gavriella-glpnet, orders two test fixes BEFORE the other eight findings, and records the review as NO-GO with 8 unresolved HIGH.
Neither ruling cites the other, so BK-STD-3 rule 2 is unmet by both and rule 6 requires the collision be raised rather than resolved by a lane.
Measured here on develop @ 59e5d5b6: glpnet-side 078 is 13/13 gn: tasks complete; all 55 open tasks are bk: (buildkit repo), so the open work is not in this repo.
The 'ship + close only' premise is falsified either way - a feature with 8 unresolved HIGH cannot be shipped and closed.
questions.impact_if_unanswered: This lane holds on 078 indefinitely and opens no era, so the single-feature era programme that Q-GLPNETA16-12 established produces nothing.

options.label: Concede 078 to gavriella-glpnet
options.consequence: Q-GLPNETS15-02 governs by BK-STD-3 rule 1 (later decided_at wins); this lane records the supersession onto Q-GLPNETA16-12, touches nothing under specs/078, and moves to the next era in Q-GLPNETA17-02.

options.label: This lane executes the two test fixes
options.consequence: ariellas-glpnet does ruling 02's tests-first work and gavriella stands down; needs an explicit handover on the channel first or two lanes edit the same suite.

options.label: Split by repo: gavriella glpnet-side, buildkit lane bk-side
options.consequence: Formalises what is already true - the 55 open tasks are bk: - and gives each repo one owner; this lane stays out of 078 entirely and the ownership record is rewritten to name two lanes.

recommendation.because: BK-STD-3 rule 1 already decides it on decided_at, gavriella has the review context and the two failing tests in hand, and the runner-up asks two lanes to coordinate an edit to one test suite mid-incident - which is the exact fork ruling 03 was written to stop.

decision.rationale: BK-STD-3 rule 1 decides it on decided_at: Q-GLPNETS15-02 (2026-09-02T14:20Z) is later than Q-GLPNETA16-12 (2026-09-01). gavriella holds the review context and the two failing tests. This lane records the supersession and touches nothing under specs/078-verification-receipts.

questions.block: No era can open on this lane until one of the three candidate features is confirmed as genuinely ship-ready.
background: Q-GLPNETA16-12 named three single-feature eras in order: 078 (WSJF 7.80), 079 madglp-writer-reader-address-discipline (5.33), 067 qr-link-provisioning (4.00), each described as 'ship + close only'.
That description is now known to be wrong for 078 (8 unresolved HIGH). It was never independently verified for 079 or 067.
Round 67 table: 079 and 067 are both state=implemented with a spec_path; 085 bk-onrestart-fleet-resume is state=specified at WSJF 7.00, ranked above both.
A prior finding on this host records 067 as having an unresolved session-blocking contract divergence and an open gavriella ownership/handshake receipt.
BK-STD-4 makes a MINOR release possible only when a roadmap feature actually reaches shipped, so no era closing means no legitimate tag from this repo.
questions.impact_if_unanswered: This lane spends the session on coordination and reporting only, produces no shipped feature, and the repo stays at tier=NONE for a third consecutive day.

options.label: Open era on 079 madglp-writer-reader
options.consequence: Highest-WSJF implemented feature with no known ownership dispute; the era starts with a codexreview to establish whether 'ship + close only' is true, rather than assuming it.

options.label: Open era on 067 qr-link-provisioning
options.consequence: Lower WSJF and carries a recorded contract divergence plus an open gavriella ownership question, so the era would likely stall at the same place 078 did.

options.label: Open era on 085 bk-onrestart-fleet-resume
options.consequence: Ranked second by WSJF and is this host's own reboot-resume machinery, but it is only specified, so the era is a full nine-stage run rather than the short close Q-GLPNETA16-12 anticipated.

options.label: Verify all three, then choose
options.consequence: Run a review pass over 079, 067 and 085 before committing, so the next era's premise is measured rather than inherited; costs a session of no shipped feature and forecloses shipping anything today.

recommendation.because: It is the highest-WSJF candidate with no ownership dispute and no recorded blocker, and opening it with a review as the first stage gets the same evidence 'verify-all-three-first' buys without spending a whole session before any work starts.

decision.rationale: 079 madglp-writer-reader-address-discipline is the highest-WSJF implemented feature with no ownership dispute and no recorded blocker. The era opens with a codexreview so the ship-and-close premise is measured rather than inherited from Q-GLPNETA16-12, which has now been falsified once.

questions.block: This lane cannot satisfy the standing order that per-phase token use be recorded in and retrieved from the takt DuckLake, because this lane cannot meter tokens.
background: The engineer standing order of 2026-08-24 requires per-phase token use to be recorded in the takt lake and RETRIEVED from it for all takt reporting, never recomputed in-process.
Q-GLPNETS15-01 measured BK-REPORT-v1 section 5 on a peer host at 24% coverage: 1282 of 5423 rows carry a token measurement, 4141 carry none, and 3069 (unphased) rows are 0/3069 measured.
The only write verb available here is buildkit-scheduler takt-tokens, and this lane has been invoking it with --method unavailable, which records honestly that a phase ran but was never metered.
A row written with --method unavailable satisfies the letter of the standing order (a row exists in the lake) while carrying no measurement, so coverage rises without any number improving.
Q-GLPNETA16-11 already ruled that a second unenforced takt write path be filed upstream; that filing is one of six ruled-but-unexecuted items on this lane.
questions.impact_if_unanswered: This lane keeps writing unmeasured rows that inflate row counts without adding measurement, and every cross-host takt comparison silently mixes measured and unmeasured rows.

options.label: Keep --method unavailable, flag coverage everywhere
options.consequence: Every takt figure this lane publishes carries an explicit measured/total coverage ratio, so an unmetered row can never be read as zero cost; no new tooling and no rival shape against Q-GLPNETS15-01.

options.label: Implement real per-phase token metering here
options.consequence: This lane builds a token counter and writes measured rows, which produces real numbers but creates a second writer into a lake whose writer defects are exactly what Q-GLPNETS15-01 assigned to @buildkit.

options.label: Stop writing unmeasured rows entirely
options.consequence: This lane writes no takt token rows until a metering path exists, which keeps the lake honest but forecloses any takt continuity for this lane across the gap and loses the phase-ran signal the rows currently carry.

recommendation.because: It is the only option that neither fabricates a measurement nor destroys the phase-ran signal, and metering locally would put a second writer into the same lake whose writer defects are already assigned to another owner.

decision.rationale: Neither fabricates a measurement nor destroys the phase-ran signal. Every takt figure this lane publishes must now carry an explicit measured/total coverage ratio. Metering locally was rejected because it would put a second writer into a lake whose writer defects are already assigned to @buildkit by Q-GLPNETS15-01.

questions.block: The mandated six-section SITREP cannot be produced on demand on this host, and this lane is under ruling not to change the generator.
background: BK-REPORT-v1 is the mandated fixed-order report and is the only sanctioned generator; its section order is explicitly not configurable.

Measured this session on ARIELLAS: one run of bk_report_v1.py all reached 1232s of CPU across 70+ minutes and had still written 0 bytes, because Python buffers redirected stdout and the report only flushes at exit.
During that window it also serialised against this lane's own roadmap round - CPU fell to ~0.2% while the round held the catalog, then resumed.
Q-GLPNETS15-03 rules that shiras publishes the patched generator and glpnet adopts it byte-for-byte and authors nothing, so this lane may not add incremental output itself.
The patched file had not appeared in the standards drop when checked at 2026-09-02T14:50Z.
questions.impact_if_unanswered: Every session either blocks for over an hour on the mandated report or publishes a SITREP that is not the mandated artefact, and both have happened.

options.label: Run it detached at session start, always
options.consequence: The report becomes the first action of every session and is ready by the time it is needed; the roadmap round must then be sequenced after it so the two do not serialise on the catalog.

options.label: Publish section 1 from roadmap_open_table.py, full report when it lands
options.consequence: The mandated roadmap table is available in seconds while sections 2-6 follow later, at the cost of two artefacts per session that a reader must reconcile.

options.label: Grant this lane an exception to add line-buffered output
options.consequence: A one-line flush change makes the report observable while running, but forecloses the single-author guarantee Q-GLPNETS15-03 exists to protect and re-opens the two-author fork it was written to close.

recommendation.because: It removes the whole latency from the critical path without touching a file this lane is forbidden to author, and unlike the partial-report option it still yields exactly one artefact in the mandated order.

decision.rationale: ENGINEER RULING, taken AGAINST this lane's recommendation. Grants ariellas-glpnet a NARROW exception to Q-GLPNETS15-03 (gavriella-glpnet, 2026-09-02T14:20Z) for line-buffered output in bk_report_v1.py only. Scope is this one change; the single-author rule otherwise stands and shiras remains the publisher. Must be cited, broadcast fleet-wide, and carried forward by any future adoption of shiras's file alongside a14f10f8.
